preamble: Answers that are part of the 2 18 of 7 5 are not further defined in their clues.

clue.text: Queen wearing glasses waves

indicators.note: what is worn sits around the wearer, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: beakers are drinking glasses or cups
R, for Regina, is the standard abbreviation for a queen

explanation.surface: A queen in spectacles waving to the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waves' looks like a royal wave, but it is the definition, read as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Large waves that crash and foam on a shore are called breakers by surfers and sailors.

clue.text: I've no profits sadly from daily recommendation of 7 5

indicators.note: something done sadly goes badly wrong, so the letters end up disordered

parts.note: taken letter for letter, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A greengrocer complains that the five-a-day advice has earned them nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 5 is the linked answer FRUIT AND VEGETABLES, so the definition reads 'daily recommendation of fruit and vegetables'.
explanation.definitionFit: Health guidance in Britain urges people to eat five servings of produce each day, the familiar 'five a day' campaign.

clue.text: Male involved in provisions for the table, right?

definitions.text: Male involved in provisions for the table, right?

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: fare is food provided for a meal
M is the standard abbreviation for male
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man has a hand in supplying food, seeking confirmation.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: read straight, it describes the man who grows our food, and the question mark flags the loose fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Growers of crops and raisers of livestock produce what ends up on our plates, so this man supplies the meal.

clue.text: Miss from Europe one's upset — female OU student

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
Rita is the heroine of the play and film Educating Rita, who studies with the Open University

explanation.surface: A young European woman is distressed, and a female distance-learning student is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: The OU is Britain's Open University, a distance-learning university; Educating Rita (Willy Russell) is about a hairdresser studying with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish speakers address an unmarried young woman with this title, the Spanish equivalent of Miss.

clue.text: See 7
A loose woman in the family

parts.note: taken as written
to loose something is to untie or release it

explanation.surface: A family's black sheep: a woman of loose morals among the relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' reads as an adjective about the woman, but it is the verb meaning to set free.
explanation.definitionFit: An auntie is a parent's sister, an affectionate name for a female relative.

clue.text: Various bugs fed alternative food

indicators.note: various means varied or diverse, so the letters come in a different order

parts.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Assorted insects were given an unusual diet in some experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: All eighteen letters of 'bugs fed alternative' are rearranged; 'food' at the end is a loose, general definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Produce from orchards and gardens forms a broad category of things we eat, so 'food' covers it.

clue.text: Compulsion of top people to appear in formal attire?

indicators.note: something that appears in a garment is wrapped inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: evening dress is formal wear
U is the old label for upper-class usage, hence top people

explanation.surface: The social pressure on the elite to turn up in evening wear.
explanation.walkthrough: U meaning upper class comes from Nancy Mitford's 'U and non-U', a British convention for posh usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is pressure or threats forcing someone to act against their will, a legal term for coercion.

clue.text: Attractive person French engineer is more or less said to be?

indicators.text: more or less said to be
indicators.note: said points to speech, and more or less admits the sounds only roughly match

parts.note: Gustave Eiffel built the Paris tower that bears his name

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a dashing French engineer counts as good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: The engineer's name, said in English, comes close to the answer, which is why the clue hedges with 'more or less'.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeful is informal for a strikingly good-looking person, someone well worth looking at.

clue.text: Poet concerned with hell putting any number off

indicators.note: putting something off means removing it, and any number is a variable letter to remove

parts.note: Dante Alighieri, Italian poet
N stands for an unspecified number in algebra

explanation.surface: A poet absorbed by the underworld keeps losing readers.
explanation.walkthrough: Dante wrote the Inferno, hence 'concerned with hell'. The answer is one of the themed fruits, so the preamble supplies its definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme is produce in the five-a-day; a date is the sweet fruit of the date palm.

clue.text: Awful matinee rot that may amuse the kids

definitions.text: Awful matinee rot that may amuse the kids

indicators.note: something awful is in a dreadful state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An afternoon show of rubbish that only children would enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes a puppet show put on at an afternoon performance, so wordplay and definition share the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A puppet worked by strings is a classic children's entertainment, often in silly afternoon shows.

clue.text: Report of an interfering type

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the answer is a sound match

parts.note: a meddler interferes in other people's business

explanation.surface: Gossip about a busybody.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a themed fruit, so the preamble supplies its definition and the whole clue is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The medlar is a small brown fruit of a tree related to the rose, eaten when half rotten.

clue.text: Began to wriggle around in truck

indicators.note: one thing set around another encloses it

parts.note: lorry is the British word for a truck

indicators.note: wriggling things twist about, so the letters squirm into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone started squirming about inside a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled letters of the first word go inside the vehicle; the answer is a themed fruit, so the preamble supplies its definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The loganberry is a hybrid of raspberry and blackberry, a red soft fruit.

clue.text: See Hindu god dance endlessly in serenade

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Shiva is the Hindu god of destruction
a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: An instruction to watch a god dancing during a love song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is the setter telling the solver to look, joined to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A shivaree is a noisy mock serenade of pots and pans given to newlyweds, a North American custom.

clue.text: Names announced — they may attract tourists

indicators.note: to announce is to speak out, so the answer is what is heard

parts.note: to cite is to name or quote

explanation.surface: A list of places is read out, each one a draw for visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Names' is a verb, meaning mentions or quotes, not a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous landmarks that visitors go to see are called the sights of a town.

clue.text: Drunk rolling over sees others like him?

indicators.note: something rolled over is turned upside down, so in a down clue its letters run backwards

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
to spot is to see

explanation.surface: A drunk falls over and notices fellow drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Him' refers back to the drunk in the clue, so the definition means other drunks, with the question mark admitting the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A tosspot is an old word for a heavy drinker, so his fellows are more of the same.

clue.text: Fast track creating bitterness at work

parts.note: gall is bitterness or rancour
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A fast-tracked promotion causes resentment in the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast track' reads as a career phrase, but it is a horse-racing track.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallop is a stretch of ground where racehorses are exercised at speed.

clue.text: See 2
New head for public school

indicators.note: a new head means the first letter is swapped for another

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public, that is private fee-paying, school

explanation.surface: An appointment of a new headteacher at a private school.
explanation.walkthrough: A British public school is an old fee-paying school. The answer is a themed vegetable, so the preamble defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: A marrow is a large green vegetable of the squash family, grown in British gardens.

clue.text: One girl swallowing another girl's white powder

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside the swallower

parts.note: Mia is a girl's name
Agnes is a girl's name

explanation.surface: One girl takes another's white powder, a little sinister.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's joins the wordplay to the definition, read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnesia, magnesium oxide, is a white powdery compound used as an antacid and laxative.

clue.text: Angel is heard — it could be on the radio

definitions.text: it could be on the radio

indicators.note: heard points to sound, so the answer matches by ear

parts.note: Ariel is an archangel in Jewish and Christian tradition and the spirit in The Tempest

explanation.surface: An angel's voice is broadcast on the wireless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the radio' suggests broadcasting, but the answer is the device sitting on top of the set.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerial, or antenna, is the rod fitted to a radio set to pick up signals.

clue.text: Small cake in larder one bridge player provided for partner

indicators.note: to provide one thing for another is to give it in place of it

parts.note: a pantry is a larder
North is one of the four players at bridge
South is North's partner at bridge

explanation.surface: A cake kept in a store-cupboard is set out by a card player for a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players are named for compass points, and North partners South.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry is also a single small baked cake or tart, as in a plate of pastries.

clue.text: What an awful smell around what's tasteless — one of the 5 not in the 2 18

definitions.text: one of the 5 not in the 2 18

indicators.note: one thing placed around another encloses it

parts.note: 'poo!' is an exclamation at a bad smell
tat is tasteless, cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone recoils at the stink of cheap junk, then a nutrition footnote.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 is VEGETABLES and 2 18 is FIVE PORTIONS: British five-a-day guidance excludes this starchy staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Health advice in Britain counts most produce but treats spuds as starch, so they don't count.

clue.text: Fire priest for being naughty maverick

indicators.note: naughty things misbehave, so the letters break out of order

parts.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A bishop sacks a priest for misbehaving and going his own way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like the verb to sack, but it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe an independent person who ignores convention and goes their own way.

clue.text: Find a king and a queen among others in this matching attire

definitions.text: Find a king and a queen among others in this
definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of the four sets in a pack of cards, each holding court cards
second meaning: jacket and trousers made of the same cloth

explanation.walkthrough: The first half sounds like royalty at a gathering, but it describes a set of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts, clubs, diamonds and spades each contain court cards, and a tailored outfit of matching pieces shares the word.

clue.text: Drunkard, passionate, wasting time repeatedly in London area

indicators.note: wasting is losing, and repeatedly means the loss happens twice over

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
T is the abbreviation for time
hot can mean passionate

explanation.surface: A lustful drunk idles away the hours in a city nightlife district.
explanation.walkthrough: The time letter goes from each of the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district in central London's West End, known for nightlife and restaurants.

clue.text: Returning soldiers transported by vehicle

indicators.note: a passenger being carried sits inside whatever carries them

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle

indicators.note: something returning comes back the way it went, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops coming home are carried in a truck.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a themed vegetable, so the preamble defines it and the whole clue is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The carrot is an orange root vegetable, a staple of the five-a-day.

clue.text: Fascinating little women being eager

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
itching to do something is being eager

explanation.surface: Charming girls who can hardly wait, perhaps a nod to Little Women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' is the abbreviation signal for women, not part of the novel's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Witching means bewitching or enchanting, holding someone under a spell.
